Summary: Core / Platform & Delivery
Description: Preserve the existing Django authentication and shared architecture while completing permissions, core settings, approved UUID numbering, planning coordination, and final integration. Authentication and all shared design/UI-UX work remain exclusively owned by Mhmd Hajeer; Malik owns planning coordination and also contributes implementation.

Summary: Coordinate the approved Phase 1 source of truth and dated delivery plan
Description: Maintain implementation traceability across the approved BRD, ERD, repository context, backlog, and team handoffs without changing scope. Estimate: 240m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Every delivery item maps to an approved BRD/ERD requirement or a documented repository gap; 2) all due dates fall from 2026-08-29 through 2026-09-06; 3) completed baseline model work is not scheduled again; 4) deferred Phase 2 features remain absent.

Summary: Provision the exact role permissions and enforce the existing authentication boundary
Description: Complete deterministic permission provisioning for Owner / Admin, Pharmacist, Inventory Manager, and Accountant while preserving Django User, sessions, AuthenticationForm login, and POST-only CSRF-protected logout. Estimate: 360m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) The four groups retain their exact names; 2) Owner / Admin receives full business permissions through its group without requiring is_superuser; 3) every protected action checks authentication and permissions server-side; 4) anonymous and unauthorized requests are denied; 5) current login, session, and logout behavior remains unchanged.

Summary: Integrate the shared application UI and permission-aware navigation
Description: Own all shared design and UI-UX integration across layouts, components, responsive behavior, navigation, dialogs, toasts, and feature-route activation. Estimate: 360m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Feature pages reuse the existing dashboard/auth layouts and documented components; 2) navigation uses the reserved namespaces and permission filtering; 3) missing routes remain safely unavailable until implemented; 4) responsive and keyboard behavior is preserved; 5) no duplicate navigation or UI framework is introduced.

Summary: Complete core settings workflow logic over the existing models
Description: Use the existing PharmacySettings, TaxRate, and PaymentMethod models to implement validation, permission-scoped handlers, and reusable form processing; do not recreate or rewrite baseline models or migrations. Estimate: 240m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Only Owner / Admin can change settings; 2) singleton pharmacy settings, one currency, tax ranges, low-stock/expiry defaults, and payment-method activation are validated; 3) secrets and environment settings are never exposed; 4) existing model constraints remain authoritative.

Summary: Deliver the core settings UI-UX
Description: Design and implement the Owner/Admin settings screens using existing forms, layouts, and shared components while keeping operational configuration separate from environment secrets. Estimate: 240m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Pharmacy identity, currency, tax, thresholds, payment methods, and invoice/receipt text are presented clearly; 2) unauthorized users cannot access change actions; 3) validation errors are accessible and preserve entered values; 4) no secret or deployment variable appears in the interface.

Summary: Implement approved UUID-derived document numbering
Description: Create one reusable service/helper for deterministic document numbers using the complete uppercase UUID hex value; no DocumentSequence model or sequence infrastructure is permitted. Estimate: 240m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Numbers use SAL-, PUR-, CRT-, SRT-, and CRF- plus the complete uppercase UUID hex value; 2) draft sales and purchase numbers may stay blank until completion/posting; 3) return/refund numbers are assigned at creation; 4) uniqueness is preserved; 5) focused tests cover every prefix and retry-safe deterministic output.

Summary: Integrate and verify the complete Phase 1 workflow
Description: Lead cross-feature integration and final technical readiness beyond authentication/design ownership, coordinating shared routes, permissions, deployment-safe configuration, and end-to-end checks. Estimate: 420m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) One representative purchase-to-stock-to-sale-to-payment-to-return/refund-to-report scenario succeeds; 2) role access matches the BRD matrix; 3) Django checks and critical tests pass; 4) no deferred purchase-order, cashier-shift, discrepancy, manual-adjustment, generic audit/idempotency, or sequence subsystem is introduced.

Summary: Coordinate final documentation and operational handoff
Description: Reconcile implementation outcomes with the BRD, ERD, repository context, development guide, Jira backlog, and Neon backup runbook; record only genuine remaining gaps and decisions. Estimate: 240m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Documentation matches the final repository state; 2) the backup runbook remains discoverable and contains no credentials; 3) migration and inventory ownership rules are explicit; 4) unresolved team-lead decisions are recorded without silently inventing requirements; 5) no completed work remains described as unimplemented.

Summary: Catalog / Inventory / Purchasing
Description: Complete catalog, party, inventory, purchase-receiving, and supplier-return workflows on the existing baseline models. All stock mutation remains inside apps.inventory; Phase 1 has no direct/manual adjustment workflow.

Summary: Expose catalog and party workflows over the existing models
Description: Implement remaining query, validation, form-processing, permission, and route logic for medicines, units, barcodes, suppliers, customers, and prescribers without rebuilding their models. Estimate: 360m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Authorized users can search and maintain approved master data; 2) unique barcodes/codes, base-unit rules, conversions, thresholds, and active-state rules are enforced; 3) used master records are deactivated rather than hard-deleted; 4) walk-in sales require no fake Customer row; 5) role permissions match the BRD matrix.

Summary: Implement authoritative inventory and FEFO services with row locking
Description: Build apps.inventory services for receiving, sale deductions, safe customer-return restocking, supplier-return deductions, FEFO eligibility, and matching StockMovement creation. No direct/manual adjustment operation is included. Estimate: 600m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Only apps.inventory changes batch quantity; 2) every mutation and movement is created in one transaction.atomic block; 3) eligible batches are locked with select_for_update in expiry_date, first_received_at, id order before quantities are rechecked; 4) expired or insufficient stock is rejected; 5) concurrent requests cannot oversell; 6) reserved manual-adjustment codes are never exposed or used.

Summary: Add the two approved stock-traceability uniqueness constraints
Description: Create reviewed follow-up migrations only for unique (sales_invoice_line, batch) allocations and unique non-null stock-movement source lines, as required by ERD Section 20; do not alter unrelated baseline fields. Estimate: 240m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) SaleBatchAllocation enforces one row per sales line and batch; 2) StockMovement enforces one movement per non-null authoritative source line using the approved conditional key; 3) migrations apply cleanly without rewriting shared history; 4) duplicate attempts fail deterministically; 5) existing valid rows remain usable.

Summary: Post purchase invoices atomically with targeted locks
Description: Implement purchase-invoice posting and receiving over existing models, using inventory services and targeted row locking; PurchaseInvoice itself is the receiving document. Estimate: 600m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Posting locks the PurchaseInvoice and each existing batch cost layer that will be increased; 2) status, totals, expiry, quantities, costs, and permissions are rechecked after locking; 3) batch increases and PURCHASE_RECEIPT movements commit atomically; 4) snapshots and balances are correct; 5) failure rolls back every write; 6) no PurchaseOrder or separate GoodsReceipt is created.

Summary: Post supplier returns against exact batches with targeted row locks
Description: Implement supplier-return posting over the existing return models, exact source batches, apps.inventory services, and targeted row locks. Estimate: 360m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Posting locks the SupplierReturn and every affected MedicineBatch before validation; 2) status and available quantities are rechecked after locking; 3) exact-batch deductions and SUPPLIER_RETURN movements commit atomically; 4) value snapshots and supplier statement effects remain traceable; 5) over-return and rollback paths are tested.

Summary: Deliver catalog, inventory, purchasing, and supplier-return UI-UX
Description: Design and implement the domain screens using the existing component system while Hala-owned services remain the business boundary. Estimate: 360m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Catalog/party maintenance, batch lookup, expiry/low-stock states, purchase posting, and supplier returns are usable on desktop and mobile; 2) permissions control visible actions; 3) batch quantity is never directly editable; 4) confirmation, error, empty, and loading states use shared components; 5) navigation uses existing namespaces.

Summary: Verify catalog, inventory, purchasing, and supplier-return behavior
Description: Add focused automated tests for the remaining domain logic and concurrency-sensitive paths; reuse existing model tests instead of duplicating baseline coverage. Estimate: 360m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Tests cover units, barcodes, deactivation, FEFO, expiry, multi-batch allocation, insufficient stock, purchase receiving, supplier returns, permissions, rollback, and movements; 2) concurrent stock tests prove targeted locks prevent lost updates/overselling; 3) no test depends on shared database state.

Summary: POS / Sales / Prescriptions
Description: Complete prescription, barcode POS, FEFO sale-completion, and invoice/receipt workflows over the existing baseline models. Malik owns domain logic and planning coordination; Mhmd Hajeer owns all domain design/UI-UX.

Summary: Deliver lightweight prescription workflows over the existing models
Description: Implement remaining prescription validation, permission, query, and request-handling logic without recreating Prescription or PrescriptionItem. Attachment upload remains disabled unless storage, access control, and retention are explicitly approved and configured. Estimate: 240m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Authorized users can create and retrieve lightweight prescriptions with optional customer/prescriber and medicine items; 2) required quantities and instructions validate; 3) POS receives non-clinical prescription-required warning data; 4) no clinical advice or complex lifecycle is added; 5) file upload is not enabled without the documented prerequisite decision.

Summary: Build server-side POS search, barcode, cart, and totals logic
Description: Implement medicine/barcode lookup, draft-sale handling, unit conversion, customer/prescription association, and authoritative Decimal preview calculations over the existing sales models. Estimate: 360m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Known barcodes resolve to the correct active medicine/unit and unknown barcodes create nothing; 2) saved and walk-in customer flows work; 3) quantities, discounts, tax, and totals are recalculated server-side using the approved rounding sequence; 4) tampered totals are rejected; 5) stock/expiry information is query-only until completion.

Summary: Complete sales atomically with deterministic FEFO row locks
Description: Implement sale completion over existing invoices/lines/allocations by calling apps.inventory and applying targeted locks and status revalidation. Estimate: 600m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Completion locks the SalesInvoice and eligible MedicineBatch rows with select_for_update in expiry_date, first_received_at, id order; 2) status, permission, totals, prescription acknowledgement, and stock are rechecked after locking; 3) allocations, negative SALE movements, cost snapshots, optional initial payment, and invoice status commit atomically; 4) insufficient/expired stock or any error rolls back all writes; 5) concurrent completions cannot oversell.

Summary: Deliver keyboard-first POS, sales, and prescription UI-UX
Description: Design and implement the server-rendered POS and prescription screens with minimal vanilla JavaScript and the existing shared components. Estimate: 360m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Barcode Enter behavior, manual search, cart editing, customer context, warning acknowledgement, stock feedback, and completion confirmation are keyboard-accessible; 2) the interface remains responsive; 3) errors preserve the cart safely; 4) no SPA or additional frontend framework is introduced; 5) permissions control visible actions.

Summary: Deliver print-ready sales invoice and receipt output
Description: Own the visual design and implementation of historically accurate HTML print views using stored invoice snapshots and shared branding. Estimate: 240m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Completed invoices display the approved number, pharmacy/customer snapshots, lines, discounts, tax, totals, payments, and balance; 2) browser print output is clean and legible; 3) later master-data edits do not change historical output; 4) PDF remains optional and cannot delay the HTML output.

Summary: Verify prescription, POS, sale-completion, and invoice behavior
Description: Add focused tests for remaining sales and prescription services, permissions, Decimal calculations, concurrency, and output data; do not duplicate baseline model tests. Estimate: 360m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Tests cover barcode lookup, walk-in/saved customers, prescription warnings, rounding, FEFO multi-batch allocation, cost snapshots, payments, rollback, and permissions; 2) concurrency tests prove deterministic locks prevent overselling; 3) invoice output uses snapshots; 4) tests create their own isolated data.

Summary: Finance / Returns / Reporting
Description: Complete payment, customer-return/refund, invoice/statement, and essential reporting workflows over the existing baseline models. Yasser owns finance/reporting logic; Mhmd Hajeer owns all domain design/UI-UX.

Summary: Post and reverse customer and supplier payments with invoice row locks
Description: Implement payment services over the existing CustomerPayment and SupplierPayment models using targeted invoice locking and approved reversal metadata. Estimate: 600m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Posting/reversal locks the affected sales or purchase invoice with select_for_update; 2) status, outstanding balance, amount, method, and permission are rechecked after locking; 3) multiple payments work without overpayment; 4) paid totals, balances, and payment status update atomically; 5) reversals retain actor/time/reason and original history; 6) concurrent payments cannot exceed the balance.

Summary: Process customer returns and refunds with targeted row locks
Description: Implement customer-return/refund services over existing models, exact sold allocations, apps.inventory restocking services, and targeted row locks. Estimate: 600m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Posting locks the CustomerReturn and every affected batch before quantity/restock validation; 2) cumulative returned quantity and refund value cannot exceed the original sale allocation/value; 3) safe non-expired items restore the original batch with a movement while unsafe/damaged/expired items do not; 4) refunds remain separate posted records and original invoice totals are unchanged; 5) all writes roll back together on failure.

Summary: Provide invoice search and derived customer/supplier statements
Description: Build permission-scoped query services over existing invoices, active payments, reversals, customer refunds, and supplier returns; do not create mutable balance or duplicate invoice tables. Estimate: 360m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Users can filter and locate sales/purchase invoices; 2) statements show chronological authoritative transactions; 3) unpaid, partial, paid, reversed-payment, refund, and supplier-return effects reconcile to invoice balances; 4) party data is isolated by permission; 5) no summary table becomes a source of truth.

Summary: Deliver the essential Phase 1 report queries
Description: Implement permission-scoped report queries for sales, purchases, inventory, low stock, near-expiry, expired stock, receivables, payables, payments, and basic COGS/gross profit using authoritative records. Estimate: 360m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Report totals reconcile to stored transactions; 2) COGS uses SaleBatchAllocation acquisition-cost snapshots; 3) inventory/expiry reports use current batches and UTC expiry rules; 4) receivables/payables reflect active payments and returns; 5) no report transaction or mutable summary model is added; 6) CSV export is attempted only after core reports pass.

Summary: Deliver finance, returns, statements, and reporting UI-UX
Description: Design and implement permission-aware screens for payments, reversals, customer returns/refunds, invoice search, statements, and reports using shared components. Estimate: 360m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Screens expose only role-permitted actions and financial detail; 2) balances, statuses, transaction chronology, conditions, refund eligibility, filters, totals, and empty states are clear; 3) destructive/effective actions require confirmation; 4) layouts are responsive and accessible; 5) no duplicate role-specific interface is created.

Summary: Verify finance, returns, statements, and report behavior
Description: Add focused tests for remaining finance/reporting logic, targeted-lock concurrency, permissions, reconciliation, and rollback; reuse baseline model tests. Estimate: 360m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Tests cover partial/multiple payments, overpayment rejection, reversals, return/refund caps, safe/unsafe restocking, statements, reports, COGS, permissions, and rollback; 2) concurrency tests prevent double payment and over-return; 3) report totals reconcile to source records; 4) tests use isolated data.

Summary: Reconcile the end-to-end financial and inventory effects
Description: Validate one representative cross-domain scenario from purchase receiving through sale, partial/full payment, customer return/refund, supplier return, balances, and reports. Estimate: 240m.
Acceptance Criteria: 1) Stock movements reconcile to batch changes; 2) sales/purchase balances reconcile to active payments and returns; 3) COGS and gross profit use stored allocation costs; 4) customer/supplier statements match invoice balances; 5) no source transaction is silently rewritten; 6) discrepancies fail the acceptance run with traceable evidence.
